section: FRBM Act - targets, escape clause, N.K. Singh Committee; fiscal consolidation path
subsections: Kelkar Task Force on FRBM implementation

accepted.s: Who chaired the Task Force on Implementation of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2004?
accepted.x: The Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act, 2004 was chaired by Vijay Kelkar.
accepted.sec: Kelkar Task Force on FRBM implementation

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a principal recommendation of the Kelkar Task Force on implementation of the FRBM Act?
o: Meeting fiscal targets mainly through monetary expansion
Financing fiscal deficits exclusively through disinvestment
Replacing all direct taxes with customs duties
Meeting fiscal targets through tax reform, widening the tax base and a comprehensive GST
accepted.x: The Kelkar Task Force emphasised tax reform, widening the tax base and introducing a comprehensive Goods and Services Tax to help meet FRBM targets.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy package linked to the committee’s mandate.
accepted.sec: Kelkar Task Force on FRBM implementation

accepted.s: Vijay Kelkar, associated with the FRBM implementation Task Force, also chaired which Finance Commission?
accepted.x: Vijay Kelkar chaired the Thirteenth Finance Commission, whose period was 2010–15.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed Finance Commission numbers.
accepted.sec: Kelkar Task Force on FRBM implementation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding deviations from fiscal targets:
1. The targets were suspended during the 2008 global financial crisis to permit fiscal stimulus.
2. During COVID-19 in 2020–21, the fiscal deficit was recorded at 9.2 per cent of GDP.
3. After COVID-19, the targets were recalibrated with a gradual return path.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Fiscal targets were suspended during the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 fiscal deficit reached 9.2 per cent of GDP in 2020–21, and a gradual return path was adopted thereafter.
accepted.tq: Check each episode separately before selecting the combined code.

accepted.s: The suspension of fiscal targets during the 2008 global financial crisis was primarily intended to facilitate:
o: An increase in statutory tax rates
A permanent abandonment of fiscal rules
accepted.x: Fiscal targets were suspended during the 2008 global financial crisis to provide room for a fiscal stimulus.
accepted.tq: Link the exceptional policy action with its stated macroeconomic purpose.

accepted.s: With reference to the COVID-19 fiscal position in 2020–21, which one of the following figures represented the fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP?
accepted.x: The fiscal deficit during 2020–21, the COVID-19 period, was 9.2 per cent of GDP.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact percentage and reject nearby fiscal-deficit figures.

accepted.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 argued for delaying strict FRBM-type targets mainly because of:
o: The complete elimination of public debt
The absence of any fiscal pressures in the States
A permanent fall in tax revenues to zero
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 supported delaying strict FRBM-type targets in view of a volatile geopolitical environment, while also warning that States’ finances were worsening.
accepted.tq: Match the policy recommendation with its stated reason.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the FRBM framework?
o: It abolished the requirement of presenting the Budget to Parliament.
It made monetary policy a function of the Finance Commission.
It transferred the power of taxation entirely to the States.
It made fiscal discipline a legal duty and created disclosure statements accompanying the Budget.
accepted.x: The FRBM framework gave fiscal discipline a legal basis and established disclosure statements as part of the Budget process.
accepted.tq: Select the option stating both linked institutional consequences.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the fiscal framework announced for Budget 2026–27:
1. It shifted the principal fiscal anchor towards a debt-to-GDP rule.
2. The debt-to-GDP target was set at 50 plus or minus 1 per cent by 2031.
3. Rolling fiscal-deficit targets continued to remain suspended.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Budget 2026–27 moved towards a debt-to-GDP anchor of 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, while rolling fiscal-deficit targets remained suspended. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Test the anchor, numerical target and status of the earlier rule together.

accepted.s: By July of FY27, the fiscal deficit was reported to be what proportion of the target in the context of Budget 2026–27?
accepted.x: The fiscal deficit by July of FY27 was reported at 26.8 per cent of the target.
accepted.tq: Use the exact quantitative figure rather than confusing it with the full-year target.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is identified as a criticism of the operation of the FRBM framework?
o: The framework imposes automatic penalties for every deviation.
The framework prohibits any deviation during crises.
An independent fiscal council is already fully operational.
Frequent use of the escape clause and repeated deferral of targets weaken credibility.
accepted.x: Frequent use of the escape clause and repeated postponement of targets are criticised for weakening the credibility of the fiscal framework. There is also no independent fiscal council yet.
accepted.tq: Find the option that states the recognised criticism rather than an institutional opposite.

accepted.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh’s fiscal position in Budget Estimates 2026–27, which one of the following is correct?
o: The fiscal deficit was 2.00 per cent, below the 3 per cent FRBM norm.
The fiscal deficit was 3.84 per cent, above the 3 per cent FRBM norm.
The fiscal deficit was 3.00 per cent, exactly equal to the FRBM norm.
The fiscal deficit was 5.84 per cent, above the 4 per cent norm.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s fiscal deficit was estimated at 3.84 per cent in BE 2026–27, which is above the 3 per cent FRBM norm.
accepted.tq: Compare the State figure directly with the benchmark norm.

accepted.s: The Fiscal Health Index of NITI Aayog ranked Andhra Pradesh at which position for 2023–24?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked 17th in the NITI Aayog Fiscal Health Index for 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Recall the rank and distinguish it from nearby ordinal positions.

accepted.s: Experts have suggested that the debt and fiscal-deficit glide path should be published along with an explicit assumption regarding:
accepted.x: Experts have called for a published debt and fiscal-deficit glide path based on an explicit nominal GDP assumption.
accepted.tq: Identify the macroeconomic variable underlying a fiscal glide path.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the newer debt anchor and the earlier FRBM framework:
1. The newer rule targets debt of 50 ± 1 per cent of GDP by 2031.
2. The new rule is criticised for tolerating a higher debt level than the 40 per cent level associated with FRBM.
3. The FRBM framework has been criticised because its targets have been missed repeatedly and it contains no penalty clause.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The new debt anchor is 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, higher than the 40 per cent level associated with FRBM, while repeated misses and the absence of a penalty clause remain criticisms.
accepted.tq: Combine the new rule with two distinct criticisms of the earlier framework.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following budgets in chronological order from the earliest to the latest:
A. First Budget in India
B. First Budget of free India
C. Budget 2026–27

Choose the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The first Budget in India was presented in 1860, the first Budget of free India in 1947, and Budget 2026–27 belongs to the latest period.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the intervening event.

accepted.s: Who presented the first Budget in India in 1860?
accepted.x: James Wilson presented the first Budget in India in 1860.
accepted.tq: Use the first-budget fact as a person–year association.

accepted.s: Who presented the first Budget of free India in 1947?
accepted.x: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Budget of free India in 1947.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first Budget in India and the first Budget after independence.
